segments.text: Before the new one: say the Malayalam for "meanwhile", then for "recently". (itiniṭe, aṭuttiṭe.) Then "once". (orikkal.)
ഈയിടെ — īyiṭe — "recently, lately".
ഈയിടെ ഞാൻ ഒരു നല്ല സിനിമ കണ്ടു. īyiṭe ñān oru nalla sinima kaṇṭu. — "Recently I saw a good film."
With a past verb it means "recently, a short while back". With a present one it means "lately, these days":
ഈയിടെ മുത്തശ്ശിക്ക് സുഖമില്ല. īyiṭe muttaśśikkŭ sukhamilla. — "Lately Grandmother has not been well."
അടുത്തിടെ, which you know, says the same. You will hear both, and a story often opens on one of them.
Its first letter is one you have not written yet. The next lesson takes it out of this word and puts it in your hand.

ഈയിടെ (īyiṭe) is native Dravidian, and it is read as "in this interval". ഈ, ī, is the "this" that stands before a noun, from the near demonstrative base (DEDR 410). ഇട, iṭa, is "interval, space between", with Tamil iṭai (DEDR 448). The -എ on the end places it in time. The same ഇട sits inside ഇതിനിടെ, "meanwhile".

lessons.title: ഈ (ī) — the letter that opens ഈയിടെ (īyiṭe)
lessons.gloss: ī — the letter that opens ഈയിടെ

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on, your eyes, for letter shapes on the page and your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Warm-up, Script you'll notice: ഈ and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Before the new one: write ഇ and ീ once each, and name them. (Short i at the start of a word; long ī after a consonant, as in വീട്.)
Now say ഈയിടെ (īyiṭe), "recently". You met it a moment ago. This lesson takes its first letter out and puts it in your hand.
ഈ — ī, a long ī, at the start of a word.
After a consonant, long ī is the sign ീ: വീട്, vīṭŭ. At the start of a word there is no consonant to carry a sign, so the vowel stands as a letter of its own, ഈ.
It is ഇ with a tail added on the right: a small lobe, a notch, and a broader lobe that sweeps back along its foot. You have read the same tail on ഊ, which is ഉ with that tail.
On its own, ഈ (ī) is also a word: "this", in front of a noun. ഈ (ī) വീട് is "this house".

One recorded hand writes ഈ (ī) in two strokes. First the whole of ഇ: from the inner tip of the small spiral, round it, up to the stem, over the broad right lobe, round the bottom, a curl below the line, and the long baseline to the right. Then, after one lift, the tail: over its small left lobe, down into the notch, over the broader right lobe, and back along its foot.
Write ഈ (ī) yourself, slowly, and larger than it is printed. Copy the printed shape, and keep the order above.

lessons.title: എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ) — and then
lessons.gloss: and then — the -ഇട്ട് you know, at the head of the next sentence

segments.text: Say "having come". (വന്നിട്ട് (vanniṭṭŭ).) Then the word for "then, after that". (പിന്നെ (pinne).)
Chapter 111 gave you the past form with -ഇട്ട് on it: "having done". Put it inside a sentence and it says "did this, and then":
ഞാൻ ചായ കുടിച്ചിട്ട് ഓഫീസിൽ പോയി. ñān cāya kuṭicciṭṭŭ ōphīsil pōyi. — "I drank tea and then went to the office."
Piece by piece: "I, tea, having drunk, to the office went". The first action is finished before the second begins.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: two sentences, with എന്നിട്ട്

segments.text: To keep the two actions as two sentences, start the second with എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ):
ഞാൻ ചായ കുടിച്ചു. എന്നിട്ട് ഓഫീസിൽ പോയി. ñān cāya kuṭiccu. enniṭṭŭ ōphīsil pōyi. — "I drank tea. And then I went to the office."
എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ) is usually explained as the -ഇട്ട് ending on the same root as എന്ന്: "having said so", "that done". It ties the next action to the one before.
പിന്നെ is the looser, everyday "then, after that", and it can also mean "later". എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ) ties the next action to the one just done.
A listener who wants the story to go on asks എന്നിട്ടോ? (enniṭṭō?), "and then?"

lessons.title: അതിനുശേഷം (atinuśēṣaṁ) — after that: a story in order
lessons.gloss: after that — and the rest of the frame a story hangs on: a time to open, first, when, finally

segments.text: Say "at first", "after", and "finally". (ādyaṁ, śēṣaṁ, oṭuvil.)
ശേഷം stands after the thing it comes after, and that thing takes -ന്. Make the thing അത്, "that", and the result is a sentence link:
അതിന് + ശേഷം becomes അതിനുശേഷം — atinuśēṣaṁ — after that.
A story then hangs on four posts: a time to open it, ആദ്യം, പിന്നെ or എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ) or അതിനുശേഷം (atinuśēṣaṁ) in the middle, and ഒടുവിൽ to close.

കഴിഞ്ഞ ശനിയാഴ്ച ഞങ്ങൾ നഗരത്തിൽ പോയി. ആദ്യം ചന്തയിൽ പോയി. അതിനുശേഷം ഒരു ചെറിയ കടയിൽ ചായ കുടിച്ചു. ഒടുവിൽ രാത്രി വീട്ടിൽ എത്തി. kaḻiñña śaniyāḻca ñaṅṅaḷ nagarattil pōyi. ādyaṁ cantayil pōyi. atinuśēṣaṁ oru ceṟiya kaṭayil cāya kuṭiccu. oṭuvil rātri vīṭṭil etti. — "Last Saturday we went to the city. First we went to the market. After that we drank tea in a small shop. Finally we got home at night."

Chapter 75 gave you വരുമ്പോൾ, "when he comes". For "when he came", take the past form you know as വന്ന and add -പ്പോൾ: വന്നപ്പോൾ (vannappōḷ). In the same way എത്തി gives എത്തിയപ്പോൾ (ettiyappōḷ), "when (I) arrived", and കണ്ടു gives കണ്ടപ്പോൾ (kaṇṭappōḷ), "when (I) saw".
ഞാൻ എത്തിയപ്പോൾ മുത്തശ്ശി കാത്തിരിക്കുകയായിരുന്നു. ñān ettiyappōḷ muttaśśi kāttirikkukayāyirunnu. — "When I arrived, Grandmother was waiting."
The -പ്പോൾ clause sets the moment; the main verb says what was going on in it, or what happened next.

lessons.title: (reading) — a visit to the village
lessons.gloss: a visit to Grandmother's village in about a hundred words — the first story in this book told in all three pasts

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: This passage is about a hundred words long. Every word in it was taught before; one new word and a few new forms are glossed after it.

ഈയിടെ (īyiṭe) ഞാൻ മുത്തശ്ശിയുടെ ഗ്രാമത്തിൽ പോയി. ആദ്യം ഞാൻ ഒരു ബസിൽ കയറി. ബസിൽ വലിയ തിരക്കായിരുന്നു. ഞാൻ ഒരു പുസ്തകം വായിക്കുകയായിരുന്നു. പെട്ടെന്ന് ബസ് നിർത്തി. ഞാൻ ഇറങ്ങി, എന്നിട്ട് (enniṭṭŭ) പതുക്കെ നടന്നു. ഞാൻ എത്തിയപ്പോൾ മുത്തശ്ശി വീട്ടിൽ കാത്തിരിക്കുകയായിരുന്നു. എന്നെ കണ്ടപ്പോൾ മുത്തശ്ശി ചിരിച്ചു. അതിനുശേഷം (atinuśēṣaṁ) ഞങ്ങൾ ചോറും മീനും തിന്നു. ഞാൻ കുട്ടിയായിരുന്നപ്പോൾ ഞങ്ങൾ എല്ലാ ദിവസവും കുളത്തിൽ കുളിക്കുമായിരുന്നു. അന്ന് ഗ്രാമത്തിൽ ഒരു ചെറിയ കട ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോൾ അവിടെ ഒരു വലിയ കട ഉണ്ട്. ഒടുവിൽ രാത്രി ഞാൻ നഗരത്തിലേക്ക് മടങ്ങി. അത് ഒരു നല്ല ദിവസമായിരുന്നു.
Read it once without stopping. Do not translate as you go; let the sentences arrive.
Then read it again and sort every verb: scene, event, or habit.
One word is new: തിരക്ക്, "a crowd, a rush", from തിരക്കുള്ള. The ending -ലേക്ക് is "to": nagarattilēkkŭ, "to the city".

The events, in order, are plain pasts of verbs you know (kayaṟi from kayaṟuka): pōyi, kayaṟi, nirtti, iṟaṅṅi, naṭannu, ciriccu, tinnu, maṭaṅṅi. The scene: vāyikkukayāyirunnu, kāttirikkukayāyirunnu. The habit: kuḷikkumāyirunnu.
